At Kalaburgi, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 09.11.2018 passed in MVC No.60/2016 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Mudigere, awarding compensation of Rs.5,24,121/- with interest at 6% p.a.

From the date of petition till realization on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in NC: 2023:KHC:40583 the road traffic accident, the Insurance Company is before this Court in appeal.

2. The case of the petitioner before the Tribunal is that, on 23.03.2015 after the completion of examination of one Kum.Sindhu, they were coming from Karkala to Singasar on the bike of his brother bearing Reg.No.KA 20/L7147 at about 3.45 PM near S.K.Border of Kudremukha-Karkala Road, the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.TN19/A-3345 came from the opposite direction with speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bike of the petitioner.

Due to which,
both the rider and pillion rider fell down from the bike and sustained injuries.
It was the further case of the petitioner that he sustained fracture of Tibia, fibula, femur of his right leg, right arm and other parts of the body.

Immediately, they were shifted to Karkala Hospital, where they took first aid and then shifted to Govt.Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore, where the petitioner Basavaraj has taken NC:
2023:KHC:40583 treatment as inpatient from 24.03.2015 to 28.04.2015 and taking treatment as outpatient regularly.

He undergone surgery to his right thigh and the plate was inserted and advised The Claim Manager vs Basavaraj B on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101131810/
2 to took rest for about 6 months.
Due to the injury he has sustained permanent disablement and now he is not in a position to walk and do any work and he spent more than Rs.5,00,000/ for medical treatment, etc.

The accident in question was solely due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN19/A3345 driven by the respondent No.1 belonging to the respondent No.2 and he was hale and healthy before accident, working as a driver under VRL Company and earning Rs.20,000/ per month and other allowances.
Hence, the respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly, severally and jointly liable to pay the compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ and prayed to allow the petition.
On issuance of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 remained absent despite service and hence they were placed exparte.
The respondent No.3-Insurance Company appeared through its counsel and filed objection statement.

The respondent No.3 denied the case of the petitioner and admits the issuance of insurance policy in the name of respondent No.2, covering the risk of the lorry bearing Reg.No.TN- 19/A3345 and respondent No.2 failed to comply Sec.134 of M.V.Act, 1988, and hence it is not liable to pay compensation and also contended that as per Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act, 1988, it is mandatory duty of the concerned police station to forward all the relevant documents to the insurance company within 30 days from the date of the information but the Sringeri Police have failed to forward the documents and not complied with the statutory demand.
There is no negligence on the part of the respondent No.1 in causing the accident and it has occurred due to the NC: 2023:KHC:40583 sole negligence of the petitioner himself.

Further it has contended that driver of the vehicle/ respondent No.1 was not having the valid driving license, the said vehicle was not having valid route permit to run in the area where the accident was taken place.

It also contended that the petitioner was not having the valid driving license to ride the motor cycle as on the date of accident and there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed appropriate issues and petitioner examined himself as PW1 and examined one witness as PW3 and Exs.P1 to P69 were marked and Ex.C1 and 2 were marked through PW3.
No oral or documentary evidence is adduced by the respondents.

5. The Tribunal after hearing both the sides and after considering the material on record, allowed NC: 2023:KHC:40583 the petition in part and awarded a sum of Rs.5,24,121/- under different heads as below and directed the insurance company to deposit the same;
 Loss of earning Rs.3,15,000/-
Pain and sufferings Rs.1,00,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 36,521/-
 Conveyance/traveling expenses Rs. 12,600/-
Attendant's charges Rs. 10,000/-

Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of amenities expenses Rs. 25,000/-

Total Rs.5,24,121/-
The Claim Manager vs Basavaraj B on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101131810/
3 6.

Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the insurance Company has approached this Court in appeal contending that, the Tribunal has not at all considered the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It was head on collision between the motorcycle and the lorry and therefore the petitioner was also equally responsible for his negligent act.

It was further contended that the Tribunal grossly erred in allowing the sum of Rs.36,521/- under the head of medical expenses when the petitioner was covered under the ESI as per Ex.P10 and therefore the medical expenses could have NC: 2023:KHC:40583 not been awarded by the Tribunal.

It was further contended that the Tribunal grossly erred in allowing a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of injury and pain and suffering and also adding future prospects while considering the compensation under the head of future prospects loss of earning capacity.
Therefore, the insurance company contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is highly exorbitant and imaginary.
7. On issuance of notice the petitioner/respondent has appeared before this Court through his counsel.

The appeal being admitted the Tribunal records has been secured and their arguments both the sides were heard.
8.
The learned counsel appearing for the appellant has reiterated the contentions raised by him in the appeal memo as noted supra.
His main NC: 2023:KHC:40583 contention is in respect of the contributory negligence and that the Tribunal could not have added future prospects while calculating the loss of earning capacity.
9. The petitioner was returning from Karkala to his village Singasar on the bike belonging to his brother along with his daughter's Sindhu.
The complaint which is at Ex.P3 discloses that he had two children and his daughter Sindhu was studying in IIIrd Standard at Karkala.

The petitioner was working as a Autorikshaw driver at Kudremukha and on 23.03.2015 his daughter Sindhu had examinations and therefore he had been to Karkala and after the examination, they stayed in the house of his brother and thereafter was returning on the motorcycle of his brother.

Near S.K.Border on Kudremukha -Karkala road, in a curving, the lorry belonging to the respondent No.1 and the offending lorry came from opposite direction - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
The petitioner and his daughter fell down and they sustained grievous injuries in the accident and the lorry driver did not stop after the accident.
Thereafter, some other commuters on the road informed his brother and taken them to the Govt. Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore.
The petitioner has produced the medical records to show the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
The wound certificate produced at Ex.P7 show that the petitioner herein had sustained fracture of the right femur, supra condylar fracture with fracture of right fibula and tibia.
The petitioner was admitted to the Govt. Wenlock Hospital at Mangalore on 24.03.2015 and was in patient till 29.04.2015.
In order to establish the disability, he examined PW3 Dr. Sudhakar.

He stated that there is shortening of the 4 cm on right lower limb with the restriction of the movement of the right knee joint and according to him disability of the petitioner is 45% to The Claim Manager vs Basavaraj B on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101131810/
4 - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 the right lower limb.
He states that there is restriction of the movement in the right knee joint.
In his cross examination he has stated that primarily he had not treated the petitioner but later he has treated him.
There is nothing on record that the PW3 had not treated the petitioner.
He was also a Orthopedic Surgeon working at Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore.
In the cross examination there is nothing which would show that his evidence is not believable.
10. Ex.P10 is the ESI temporary identity certificate and it shows that the petitioner was employed with VRL Logistics.
The date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 05.05.1973.
It is pertinent to note that there is nothing in Ex.P10 which shows that he was a driver at VRL.
However, the petitioner has not produced driving licence belonging to him.
It has come in the oral testimony of the PW1 that he was a driver at VRL for sometime.

However, in the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 complaint it is mentioned that in the year 2015 when the accident took place,
he was the autoriskhaw driver at Kudremukha.
The above evidence discloses that the petitioner was not lorry driver but he was an autorikshaw driver at Singasar of Kudremukha.
If at all the petitioner was the driver of the VRL, he could have produced the income proof by way of salary certificate.
Therefore there is nothing on record to show that he was still working as an employee under the VRL Logistics.

11. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant-insurance company contends that when Ex.P10 ESI certificate produced by him, the petitioner is entitled for a compensation of the medical expenses from the ESI Hospital and therefore ESI Authorities and therefore medical expenses could not have been granted by the Tribunal.

There is nothing on record as on the date of the accident, the petitioner was still a - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 contributed of the ESI and he had availed the facility under the Employees State Insurance Act.
Therefore, this contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant cannot be accepted.

12. The second contention of learned counsel for the appellant is that the petitioner has contended that he was working as a driver and earning Rs.20,000/- from VRL and no documentary evidence is available.

Of course, the contention of the petitioner had been considered by the Tribunal but it has not accepted the income of the petitioner at Rs.20,000/- However, it has considered the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.10,000/-.
It is pertinent to note that the accident occurred in the year 2015 and therefore the notional income of Rs.10,000/- is also on the higher side.

Though the petitioner contended that he was working as an Authorikshaw driver in the FIR,
- 14 - The Claim Manager vs Basavaraj B on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101131810/
5 NC: 2023:KHC:40583 there is nothing on record to show that he owned any autorikshaw.
13. The guidelines issued by the KSLSA for the purpose of settlement of the disputes before the Lok- Adalat prescribed a notional income of Rs.9,000/- for the year 2015.
In umpteen numbers of decisions, this Court has held that the notional income prescribed by the KSLSA is in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of Rs.9,000/- has to be accepted by this Court.
14. The learned counsel contends that the addition of 25% towards the future prospects to the notional income is not warranted and therefore the impugned judgment is erroneous.

The evidence of the PW3 discloses that the disability to the right lower limb of the petitioner for having sustained the fracture of the femur and the fracture of fibula and tibia has - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 resulted in a disability of 45% to the right lower limb.
Considering the fact that the petitioner was driver of the autorikshaw and that he was a former employee of VRL, it can be stated that the petitioner is unable to work as a driver with ease.
Definitely the injuries suffered by him to the femur and the both the bones of the right leg is going to cause disability to him.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the functional disability of the petitioner has to be taken at 25%.
The Tribunal has simply considered 1/3rd of the disability of the limb as stated by PW3 to be the functional disability.
There is no reference to the avocation of the petitioner as contended by him.
Under these circumstances, the functional disability has to be considered at 25%.
Since the disability is less than 50%, there is no need for considering the future prospects.
If the disability is drastically affecting the earnings of the petitioner, then the loss of future prospects could have been added.
Moreover, no fixed - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 income is shown by the petitioner.

Therefore, the loss of earning capacity of the petitioner is calculated as Rs.9,000/- x 12 x 14 x 25% = Rs.3,78,000/-.
15.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of pain and suffering to the extent of Rs.1,00,000/- on account of the above injuries sustained for the right lower limb appears to be on the higher side.

The same is assessed by this Court at Rs.50,000/-.
16.

The Tribunal has awarded a compensation of Rs.36,521/- towards the medical expenses and in the absence of any material to show that the petitioner had availed the facility under the ESI Act, it is not possible for this Court to hold that the petitioner is to be deprived of the said amount.
Simply because he held certificate of ESI for the year 2013, it cannot be said that the medical expenses could not be awarded to him.

- 17 - The Claim Manager vs Basavaraj B on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101131810/
6 NC: 2023:KHC:40583 17.

The Tribunal has also awarded a sum of Rs.12,600/- under the conveyance and traveling expenses, a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the attendant charges, a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards future medical expenses and Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amentias in life.
No enhancement or reduction is required in this quantum of the compensation.
18. The next contention raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the petitioner also contributed for the negligence.
It is evident from the police papers that the police have filed the charge sheet against the lorry driver insured by the respondent No.3-appellant.
The damages suffered to the lorry indicate that there was a dent on the front right side bumper.
Similarly the right indicator of the motorcycle was also damaged in the accident.
It is pertinent to note that the contributory negligence - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 cannot be inferred in the absence of any cogent evidence.
Obviously the accident has occurred in a curving and it is evident that the lorry had gone on the extreme right side while taking the left turn.
Thus it is evident that the driver of the lorry should have been more cautious while driving the vehicle in a curving.
The petitioner was on a two wheeler and there is absolutely no material on record to show that there was any negligence on the part of the petitioner.

19. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner has contended that the insurance company has not raised any dispute in respect of the claim petition filed by the daughter of the petitioner and therefore there is no reason for the insurance company to raise a contention of contributory negligence in the present case.
Obviously it was a case of composite negligence for her.
The available evidence on record, in no way show that there was - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Simply because the petitioner has not produced his driving licence, it cannot ipso facto prove that there was contributory negligence on the part of petitioner.
This contention of the appellant regarding the contributory negligence cannot be accepted.
Consequently, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part and the findings of the Tribunal that 25% has to be added towards the loss of future prospects cannot be accepted.

However, on the re-appreciation and reassessment of the compensation, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as below:
Loss of future earning Rs.3,78,000/-
 Pain and sufferings Rs.50,000/-

Medical expenses Rs. 36,521/-
 Conveyance/traveling expenses Rs. 12,600/-
 Attendant's charges Rs. 10,000/-

Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000/-
The Claim Manager vs Basavaraj B on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101131810/
7  Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/-

The above sum being the just and proper compensation, though the appeal deserves to be - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:40583 allowed in part by rejecting the addition of future prospects, the compensation needs to be enhanced marginally.
Hence, the appeal is partly allowed and the compensation is enhanced to Rs.5,37,121/-.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeal is allowed in part.

The petitioner-respondent No.2 is entitled for compensation of Rs. Rs.5,37,121/-
instead of Rs.5,24,121/- as awarded by the Tribunal, along with the interest at the rate 6% per annum from the date of petition till its deposit before the Tribunal.
The amount in deposit before this Court is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal.
